headline: MRVL +9.85% after Marvell handed Google a warrant over $12.2bn of its own stock, the largest rise of the twelve.
quick: Marvell told the market how big Google intends to get, and rose 9.85%. It disclosed on 19 August a warrant giving Google up to 58,970,907 shares at $206.58, worth $12.18bn. Almost all of it vests only as Google buys, one tranche per $500m of revenue. That was the largest rise of the twelve, on the heaviest volume of the twelve at 196% of average.

Nebius sold $5bn of convertible notes and fell 9.87%. It proposed $4.5bn on the morning of 19 August and priced an upsized $5.0bn after the close. Both conversion premiums are struck off a reference price of $223.90, which is exactly Wednesday's close. That was the largest fall of the twelve, and its third multi-billion convertible in under a year.

The Treasury moved to cap long borrowing costs, and nine of the twelve rose. It said it will at least double its buybacks of 10 to 30-year debt, from $2bn to $4bn per operation, from 9 September. The 30-year yield eased to about 5.285% from a 19-year high. QQQ still closed -0.20% against SPY at +0.21%.

macro.dt: The Treasury said on 19 August it will at least double its liquidity buybacks of 10 to 30-year securities, from $2bn to at least $4bn per operation, starting 9 September. The 30-year yield fell more than 2 basis points to about 5.285%, after setting a 19-year high of 5.33% the day before
macro.dd: A buyback is the government bidding for its own long debt. That puts a buyer under the part of the curve that sets the discount rate on profits expected years out. Most of what investors pay for NBIS, PLTR, TSLA and MRVL is exactly that kind of profit. A smaller discount rate raises the present value of a distant dollar more than a near one, which is why six of the twelve rose 1% or more.

macro.dt: The Federal Reserve published its July minutes at 14:00 ET on 19 August, and they read hawkish. Several officials favoured a rise, and many said more tightening may be needed if inflation does not fall. The July decision held rates at 3.50-3.75% with three dissents, all for a 25bp increase
macro.lead: Why the two macro items point opposite ways
macro.dd: The Treasury acts on the long end, the Fed on the short end. Buybacks lowered the cost of waiting, minutes raised the odds that money stays expensive. The rally that followed the open faded through the afternoon, which is what a market splitting the difference looks like. Neither changed a single company's revenue.

macro.dt: QQQ closed -0.20% while SPY closed +0.21%, and nine of these twelve rose. Premarket this morning has QQQ at +0.01% and SPY at -0.02%
macro.dd: The index fell on a day when three quarters of this list rose. That gap comes from the rest of the Nasdaq-100, not from these twelve. Read it as a warning that the rate relief was narrow: it reached the names priced on distant profits and left the index flat. Premarket is flat and thin, so today's open decides it, not the futures.

entries.strength_label: Major move · capital raise · company event
entries.happened: Nebius proposed $4.5bn of convertible notes on Wednesday morning, then priced an upsized $5.0bn after the close.
figures: $3.0bn of 0.50% notes due 2030 convert at about $313.46, a 40% premium. $2.0bn of 4.50% notes due 2034 convert at about $324.65, a 45% premium
Both premiums are struck off a reference price of $223.90. That is exactly Wednesday's close. Purchasers hold an option on $750m more, and settlement is 24 August
This is the third multi-billion convertible in under a year, after $2.75bn and $4.0bn. Capital spending guidance for 2026 is $20bn to $25bn, so $5bn funds roughly a quarter of one year
Closed $223.90, -9.87%, the largest fall of the twelve. The intraday range of 9.66% was the widest of the twelve. Volume ran at 160% of average
entries.why: A convertible is a share sale with the date left open. Holders are diluted only if the stock reaches the conversion price, so the cost is contingent rather than booked today. What the market repriced is the pace. Three raises in a year, against building that costs $20bn to $25bn a year, says the contracts already signed do not pay for the capacity they require.

foot.v: Wednesday's settled 9.87% fall priced the morning's $4.5bn proposal only. The final size and terms landed after the bell, so that close does not contain them. Premarket has NBIS at +1.30%, the second largest premarket rise of the twelve. Treat that as provisional: the open settles it.
Nebius names a contract whose prepayments cover a full year of capital spending, removing the need for a fourth raise.
24 August, settlement. Third quarter results are expected around 10 November.

entries.happened: Marvell disclosed on 19 August that it has issued Google a warrant over 58,970,907 of its shares.
figures: The exercise price is $206.58, worth $12.18bn if fully exercised. The warrant was issued 18 August and runs to 18 August 2033
Only 1,360,867 shares vest on time, in equal quarterly instalments over the first year. The remaining 57.6m vest in 240 tranches, one for every $500m of custom-product revenue Google generates

Full vesting therefore needs $120bn of Google revenue between Marvell's fiscal third quarter of 2027 and the end of fiscal 2033. Marvell's entire first quarter revenue was $2.418bn, and it guided the second to $2.7bn

The underlying commercial agreement was signed 29 July. It covers AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, network and memory interface controllers, and near-memory compute for Google's TPU ecosystem
Closed $237.27, +9.85%, the largest rise of the twelve, on 196% of average volume, the heaviest participation of the twelve
entries.why: The vesting schedule is the disclosure, not the warrant. Marvell has published the scale of business its new customer is planning, in a number it had no other way to state. That turns a supplier relationship into something nearer backlog (revenue already under contract), which is what earns a durable multiple. It also caps the upside, because every tranche of that revenue hands Google stock at a fixed price.

foot.v: Wednesday's settled close rose 9.85%, so the disclosure was taken seriously. It stops well short of the implied revenue, which on any multiple would be worth far more than 10%. The market is weighting the condition, not the headline number. Premarket today is -0.54%, provisional and thin.
Guidance on 27 August shows custom-silicon revenue tracking below the $500m-per-tranche pace, which would make the warrant a ceiling rather than a signal.
27 August, second quarter results, one day after Nvidia.

entries.strength_label: Minor move · two dated capital events · the asymmetry
entries.happened: Alphabet sold its first Australian dollar bonds on 19 August and took the Marvell warrant on the same day.
figures: It sold A$5.5bn, about $3.9bn, in a multi-part deal. The 20-year tranche priced at 6.98%, its highest yield on any note it has issued. Demand exceeded A$18bn
The Marvell warrant cost it no cash at all. It pays for chips in Marvell's stock, not its own money
Closed $344.72, +0.15%, on 93% of average volume, and sits 15.6% below its 52-week high
entries.why: Nearly 7% for twenty-year money is the hurdle rate every data centre Alphabet now builds has to clear. It also explains the warrant on the same day. When cash is the expensive input, paying a supplier in that supplier's own equity costs nothing at signing. Watch for the structure to spread, because it moves the funding cost off the buyer's balance sheet entirely.

foot.v: A 0.15% close on two dated capital events is a non-reaction. The market is treating the borrowing cost as the sector's problem rather than Alphabet's, and is not yet pricing the warrant as a cost. Premarket is -0.24%, provisional.
A second hyperscaler writes a supplier warrant on similar terms, which would confirm the structure as a template rather than a one-off.
28 October, third quarter results.

entries.strength_label: Major move · no company event · dilution overhang
entries.happened: Intel fell 4.02% with no company announcement dated 19 August, a second heavy day.
figures: Closed $92.80, 2.3% below the $95 at which it sold 210,526,315 shares. That offering priced on 10 August and closed 12 August, so it is not an event in this window
The raise was upsized to $20bn from $15bn and drew roughly $100bn of orders. Net proceeds were about $19.7bn. Underwriters hold a 30-day option on 31,578,947 more shares
It sits 34.8% below its 52-week high, the second largest gap of the twelve. Volume was 98% of average, so this was steady selling rather than a rush
entries.why: New shares dilute for as long as the money they raised earns less than the old shares did. Intel is putting the proceeds into foundry capacity that produces no revenue for years, so earnings per share fall now and the return arrives later. A price below the issue price also means the buyers of that placement are underwater, and that tends to keep supply coming.

foot.v: There was no news to price. Set against QQQ's 0.20% fall, a 4.02% decline is a stock-specific overhang working itself out, not a sector move. Premarket is +0.02%, which is no information at all.
A foundry customer commits with a dollar value attached, which would let the capacity spending be read as backlog rather than as cost.
22 October, third quarter results.

entries.strength_label: Major move · no company event · sector
entries.happened: Robinhood rose 4.63% on a crypto and brokerage sector move, with no filing or contract behind it.
figures: Closed $95.77 on 166% of average volume. Rival brokers and crypto-linked names rose with it, which is the tell. Bitcoin held near $68,000 as long yields eased
Its chief executive called publicly for US regulators to permit tokenised stocks. That is advocacy, not a filing, a contract or a rule change
It sits 37.8% below its 52-week high, the largest gap of the twelve. Premarket today is +4.73%, the largest premarket move of the twelve
entries.why: Robinhood's revenue is a geared bet on how much retail money changes hands, and crypto trading is the highest-margin part of it. An easing discount rate and a firm coin price lift the volume assumption and the multiple at the same moment. Nothing inside the business changed on Wednesday.

foot.v: Wednesday's 4.63% is a settled close on a sector input, roughly twenty-three times QQQ's move in the opposite direction. Today's +4.73% premarket is thin and provisional, and premarket moves in this name reverse often. The open settles it.
The SEC publishes an innovation exemption with terms attached, which would turn advocacy into a dated regulatory event.
4 November, third quarter results, estimated.

entries.strength_label: Major move · permit filings · no company statement
entries.happened: Tesla rose 4.23% on Cybercab logistics visible in permit filings, not on any company announcement.
figures: Permits show a leased site on St Elmo Road in Austin and plans for 80 wireless chargers for the Cybercab fleet
China wholesale sales reached 561,528 units year to date, about 29.9% ahead of the same period last year
Closed $351.12 on 113% of average volume, and sits 29.6% below its 52-week high. Premarket is -0.72%, the weakest premarket reading of the twelve
entries.why: Charger permits are the first physical evidence that a driverless fleet has somewhere to park and recharge. That moves a robotaxi from a statement into a schedule, and a shorter wait is worth more than a longer one at any discount rate. It still changes no revenue line this year.

foot.v: A 4.23% settled close on filings that carry no dollar value is the market paying for timing, not for earnings. Today's premarket gives some of it back, which is provisional and thin.
Austin regulators set a condition that delays paying passengers, or Tesla confirms a permit for public paid rides.
21 October, third quarter results.

entries.strength_label: Minor move · press report · results in six days
entries.happened: Nvidia was reported to be weighing an investment in Mercor at a $20bn valuation, with no filing to confirm it.
figures: Closed $217.56, -0.99%, on 96% of average volume. It sits 8.0% below its 52-week high, the second smallest gap of the twelve
It reports second quarter results on 26 August after the close, confirmed by the company. That is the nearest results date of the twelve, with Marvell one day behind it
entries.why: A reported minority stake in a private company changes no revenue line, so this block is really about the date six days out. Next week's guidance sets the capital spending assumption that MRVL, INTC and NBIS are all priced against. A quiet week here is the calm before the number that reprices its suppliers.

foot.v: A 0.99% fall on average volume, six days before results, is positioning rather than a reaction. Premarket is +0.44%, provisional.
Nvidia files an 8-K confirming the Mercor investment with terms, which would make it a data event rather than a report.
26 August, second quarter results after the close.

entries.strength_label: Minor move · litigation running · not new
entries.happened: The youth safety trial in Oakland federal court continued, having opened on 18 August.
figures: Four states are arguing the case, from the 29 that sued in 2023. The claims include gathering data on under-13s without parental consent
The states have told the court they will seek damages of about $200bn, and they also want changes to how Facebook and Instagram operate
Closed $546.03, +0.43%, on 110% of average volume. It sits 31.0% below its 52-week high
entries.why: The damages figure is a demand, not an award, and courts rarely grant the number asked for. The operating remedies matter more: a ruling that changes how minors are ranked and recommended would hit engagement, and engagement is what Meta sells. That is a revenue risk, not a one-off charge.

foot.v: Opening arguments were 18 August, so Wednesday's 0.43% is not a reaction to them. The market is pricing a long trial with no near-term cash consequence. Premarket is +0.54%, provisional.
The court signals it will consider structural remedies, rather than damages alone.
Daily, through a trial expected to run four to six weeks from 18 August.

entries.happened: Microsoft trades without its dividend today, a mechanical adjustment rather than news.
figures: The quarterly dividend is $0.91 a share, declared on 10 June and payable 10 September. Today is both the record date and the ex-dividend date
That removes about 0.19% from the price at the open by arithmetic alone
Closed $484.31, +0.56%, on 76% of average volume, the lightest participation of the twelve
entries.why: Worth flagging only so a small fall at the open is not misread as a reaction. The declaration is over two months old and the rate is unchanged, so nothing here moves growth, margins or cash flow. Microsoft usually announces its annual dividend increase in September, and that is the next number that matters.

foot.v: Nothing to price. The lightest volume of the twelve on a day when nine rose is the market ignoring this name. Premarket is +0.14%.
September brings a dividend increase materially above the recent pace, or none at all.
28 October, first quarter results, estimated.

readthrough.title: The asymmetry: two companies raised money on the same day and were treated in opposite ways
readthrough.body:
Alphabet borrowed A$5.5bn and closed up 0.15%. Nebius raised $5bn and fell 9.87%. Alphabet paid the higher headline rate, 6.98% on its 20-year tranche against coupons of 0.50% and 4.50% at Nebius. The cheaper money got the worse reception.

The difference is what the money is promised out of. Alphabet's bond is repaid from cash it already earns, so an expensive coupon is a cost and nothing more. Nebius's converts are repaid in shares if the stock rises and in cash it does not yet generate if it does not. A low coupon on a convertible is not cheap financing. It is the price of selling equity later, and the market prices the equity, not the coupon.

The read-through is the Marvell warrant. GOOGL paid a supplier in that supplier's own stock and paid no cash at all, on the same day it discovered what twenty-year money costs. Expect that structure to spread across MSFT, AMZN and META, because it moves the funding cost off the buyer entirely. For MRVL, NVDA and INTC that is the question underneath every order book: whether the customer is paying with money or with your own shares.

note.title: What was quiet, what was excluded as old, and what could not be checked
note.body:
Nothing material. AAPL +2.19%, AMZN +2.46% and PLTR +2.13% had no company announcement dated 19 August. All three moved with the long-end rate relief and nothing else. Amazon and Palantir traded below their own average volume, which is what a rate move rather than a company move looks like.

Excluded as old. Intel's $20bn share sale priced 10 August and closed 12 August. Apple's cut in EU commission to 26% was 18 August and appeared in yesterday's edition. Amazon's $11.57bn agreement to buy Globalstar dates from 14 April. The Pentagon memo directing up to $243.9m to Palantir is dated 4 August. Microsoft's dividend was declared 10 June. Palantir's second quarter revenue of $1.9bn was reported in early August. All of these recirculated in the past 24 hours as though they were new.

Could not be checked. sec.gov is blocked from this environment, so Marvell's 8-K and Nebius's 6-K could not be read directly. Their figures are taken from the companies' own releases as carried by the coverage, and the warrant share count and exercise price agree across every source seen. Nebius's press release could not be opened directly either: one headline gives the priced size as $4.0bn and the rest give $5.0bn, and the $5.0bn figure is used here because the tranche detail is consistent with it. The Treasury buyback and Fed minutes details come from press reporting of the releases.

A note on price windows. Every percentage is Wednesday 19 August's settled close unless labelled premarket. Premarket quotes were available this morning and are stamped between 08:41Z and 11:02Z. They are thin, they reverse often, and none of them is a reaction the market has settled on.
